text: Hi, welcome to This is My Architecture. I have with me Satish from ZS Associates.
Hi Satish, welcome to This is My Architecture. Hi Rahul, thanks for having me.
Hey, great. So Satish, tell us something about ZS Associates and your role there.
Sure. So ZS Associates is a global professional services firm. We pride ourselves in solving
some of our clients most difficult and complex sales and marketing problem. At ZS we have
strategy, we have consulting, we have technology and operations. Operations is where I sit and
I drive intelligent process automation which is what we will be discussing here. We will
be discussing cognitive automation that you have here and robotic process automation.
Great. So what is the business challenge you were looking to solve here?
Sure. So automation has been a very key focus for ZS for a very long time. Starting 2017,
we onboarded something called robotic process automation into as a building block for our
solutions. And our initial assumption, our initial approach was that one size will fit all. But
very soon we realized that that was not the case. What we saw from our management services
business that based upon the maturity of the team's understanding, they were looking for higher level
of autonomy, higher level of control. And that required us to provide different sort of access privileges,
security accesses, and different sort of classification and logical separation of these environment for them.
So it seems like you were tailoring the controls and restrictions that you placed on the various teams within
ZS. So can you go over the architecture that you used to implement this?
Absolutely. So robotic process automation uses these bots. Bots are essentially the way to mimic human action,
to perform any processes as long as you can define it within some rules. So you need to trigger these bots. What we have here is,

you can have these bots triggered manually. In some cases we do that. Where a user either sends an email or puts a file into a S3 bucket or there is some automated way within which the file is updated in the S3 bucket. That then
triggers the bot to then perform a business process end to end or even in some cases just a task of a bigger business process.
Which RPA tools have you been using for bots?
So this architecture, Adzs, is built on Automation Anywhere. But we also then, for our clients, work on UiPath and Blue Prism.
Tell me what the bots do exactly.
Yes, so we have two kinds of bot machine. One is our control room, which basically manages the orchestration of the bots. The second is the actual bots. And based on the use case,

based on the use cases, we have different kinds of machine. Based on the processing requirement, compute requirement for a particular use case, we use various kinds of machines which function as our bots.
And what about the rules?

Yes, so this is where, this is the secret sauce of the whole architecture. The rules are the language which the bots understand to take any action. So we have defined languages within Automation Anywhere software to then take action as per the trigger signal. So what will happen is the bots, based upon the trigger, will then interact with the bots.

Interact with the RDS database here. Understand what are the rules that are to be needed to perform an end-to-end business process and then execute on them. Also get the right privileges and access from the database itself.
So when you say execute, what does that mean here for the bots?

Sure. So based upon the rules and based upon the use case, we have multiple flavors to this. We use VPC pairing, VPN tunnels, to access client applications, sometimes enterprise applications, execute a process end-to-end.
Then have this feedback loop between the trigger and action.

Seems like it's very interesting that you say you want you're using VPC pairing to connect with client applications. Is security such an important factor? Are your clients in industries that are regulated?

Absolutely. So security data privacy is top of our mind in these use cases. All of our use cases have a very heavy component of security. We need to ensure that the right level of access, the right level of privileges are passed on to the user to perform a particular set of application.
Okay. So I see that you've been using a lot of cognitive services. Can you tell us how these add into the solution?

Sure. So we have been on this automation journey for a while now. And since last November 2018, we started to experiment with transcribe and comprehend initially. One of our use cases I can talk about where we do audio translations for our customers.
So the audio files are then put into the S3 bucket, which are then transcribed. We then apply comprehend to extract keywords. In some of the use cases, we also do text to speech using poly.

And then these outputs are then feed into the bots to then apply more business rules to drive these use cases more end to end. So we use the output. We use bots to transform these outputs, apply the rules, business rules that are there, and then deliver to our clients, to our teams that are then looking for these answers.
That's amazing stuff, Satish. Can you also tell us what the future holds for this solution?

Sure. So we are very excited with our journey so far. We remain very excited with the things that are happening in the world with automation. We are going to continue pushing the envelope with automation, continue driving more value for our customers and for ourselves.
That's amazing, Satish. Thank you for joining us here and sharing your architecture with us.
It's a pleasure.
Thank you.
Thank you for joining us for This is My Architecture.
